extracted.subtask_description: Reporting on military equipment, operations and wartime events for a general newspaper audience; pieces must respect wartime censorship while using human-interest details (pilot quotes, unit records) to convey significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on describing classified details
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not permitted to describe details of the Typhoon's appearance, armament or performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Typhoon was shown to press representatives, reporters must withhold specifics about appearance, armament and performance. Reporters should instead rely on permitted content such as pilots' impressions and high-level statements about the aircraft's role or effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use veteran pilots' testimony and unit records to convey effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of past performance showed the reporters why veteran pilots have lost their hearts to this new fighter; many pilots who have flown it think it is superior to the Spitfire for many fighting jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When technical details are restricted, use first-hand pilot quotes, loss/kill ratios, squadron composition and mission summaries to illustrate capability (e.g., pilots' statements like 'the Typhoon is faster than anything Jerry has and it packs a hell of a punch', squadron tallies of enemy planes destroyed and losses). Present comparative and anecdotal evidence (unit records, mission outcomes) to support claims while avoiding prohibited technical specifics.
